metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Settings and Options
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Settings and Options APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers the option-backed setting 'wpbp_setting_title' in the 'wpbp' group as a REST-exposed string setting whose saved value is sanitized as plain text.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_settings_options_001()` registers `wpbp_setting_title` with `register_setting()` in the `wpbp` group, exposes it through REST settings metadata, declares string data, and registers a sanitizer that strips markup. Runtime validation inspects WordPress's registered settings registry and verifies that `sanitize_option()` applies the registered sanitizer.
requirements: Use the Settings API
Register the setting under group 'wpbp' with option name 'wpbp_setting_title'
Expose the setting to REST clients and sanitize stored values as plain text

required_patterns.description: Registers a sanitizer for saved values

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_001' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_settings_options_001(); global $wp_registered_settings; if ( empty( $wp_registered_settings['wpbp_setting_title'] ) ) { return false; } $setting = $wp_registered_settings['wpbp_setting_title']; $rest = $setting['show_in_rest'] ?? false; $rest_ok = true === $rest || ( is_array( $rest ) && isset( $rest['schema'] ) ); return 'wpbp' === ( $setting['group'] ?? null ) && 'string' === ( $setting['type'] ?? null ) && $rest_ok && isset( $setting['sanitize_callback'] ) && is_callable( $setting['sanitize_callback'] ) && 'Title' === sanitize_option( 'wpbp_setting_title', 'Title' );
assertions.description: The setting is registered as a REST-exposed sanitized string setting

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_001(): void { register_setting( 'wpbp', 'wpbp_setting_title', array( 'type' => 'string', 'show_in_rest' => true, 'sanitize_callback' => 'sanitize_text_field', 'default' => '' ) ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that creates the 'wpbp_noautoload' option with a provided value sanitized as plain text and excluded from WordPress autoloading, returning whether the option was added.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_settings_options_002()` adds `wpbp_noautoload` with `add_option()`, stores the provided value after plain-text sanitization, and disables autoloading using the modern Options API behavior. Runtime validation checks the stored value and confirms the options table autoload marker is not one of WordPress's autoloaded values.
requirements: Use the Options API
Store the sanitized value in 'wpbp_noautoload'
Disable autoloading for the option

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_002' ) ) { return false; } global $wpdb; $added = wpbp_settings_options_002( 'Value' ); $stored = get_option( 'wpbp_noautoload' ); $autoload = $wpdb->get_var( $wpdb->prepare( "SELECT autoload FROM {$wpdb->options} WHERE option_name = %s", 'wpbp_noautoload' ) ); $autoloaded_values = function_exists( 'wp_autoload_values_to_autoload' ) ? wp_autoload_values_to_autoload() : array( 'yes' ); return true === $added && 'Value' === $stored && is_string( $autoload ) && ! in_array( $autoload, $autoloaded_values, true );
assertions.description: The option is stored sanitized and is not marked for autoloading

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_002( string $value ): bool { return add_option( 'wpbp_noautoload', sanitize_text_field( $value ), '', false ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that updates the 'wpbp_nested' option by storing a supplied plain-text-sanitized value under a supplied sanitized key, preserving existing entries, and returning the full updated option array.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_settings_options_003()` reads the existing `wpbp_nested` array with `get_option()`, normalizes the supplied key with `sanitize_key()`, sanitizes the supplied value as plain text, persists the updated array with `update_option()`, and returns the same persisted array. Runtime validation seeds an existing entry, checks preservation, and verifies the sanitized key and value in both the return value and stored option.
requirements: Use the Options API to read and update 'wpbp_nested'
Sanitize the supplied key and value before storing
Preserve existing option entries

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_003' ) ) { return false; } $out = wpbp_settings_options_003( 'Some Key!', 'Value' ); $stored = get_option( 'wpbp_nested' ); return is_array( $out ) && is_array( $stored ) && array( 'existing' => 'keep', 'somekey' => 'Value' ) === $out && $out === $stored;
assertions.description: The nested option is updated with sanitized data while preserving existing entries

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_003( string $key, string $value ): array { $options = get_option( 'wpbp_nested', array() ); if ( ! is_array( $options ) ) { $options = array(); } $options[ sanitize_key( $key ) ] = sanitize_text_field( $value ); update_option( 'wpbp_nested', $options ); return $options; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that registers a settings section 'wpbp_section' and a settings field 'wpbp_field' on the built-in 'reading' settings page, with the field assigned to that section.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_settings_options_004()` uses the Settings API to register `wpbp_section` on the `reading` page and `wpbp_field` inside that section. Runtime validation inspects the Settings API globals populated by `add_settings_section()` and `add_settings_field()` and checks that both callbacks are callable.
requirements: Use the Settings API
Register the section and field on the 'reading' settings page
Assign the field to the registered section

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_004' ) ) { return false; } wpbp_settings_options_004(); global $wp_settings_sections, $wp_settings_fields; $section = $wp_settings_sections['reading']['wpbp_section'] ?? null; $field = $wp_settings_fields['reading']['wpbp_section']['wpbp_field'] ?? null; return is_array( $section ) && is_array( $field ) && 'wpbp_section' === ( $section['id'] ?? null ) && 'wpbp_field' === ( $field['id'] ?? null ) && is_callable( $section['callback'] ?? null ) && is_callable( $field['callback'] ?? null );
assertions.description: The requested section and field are registered on the reading page

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_004(): void { add_settings_section( 'wpbp_section', 'WPBP Settings', '__return_null', 'reading' ); add_settings_field( 'wpbp_field', 'WPBP Field', '__return_null', 'reading', 'wpbp_section' ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that deletes a supplied option name and then returns WordPress's fallback value for that option using a supplied fallback.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_settings_options_005()` deletes the supplied option name with `delete_option()` and then returns `get_option()` using the supplied fallback, without creating or reseeding the option itself. Runtime validation creates the fixture option before execution, checks that the fallback is returned after deletion, and verifies the option no longer exists.
requirements: Use the Options API
Delete the provided option name
Return get_option() with the provided fallback after deletion

forbidden_patterns.description: Does not recreate the option before deleting it

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_005' ) ) { return false; } $result = wpbp_settings_options_005( 'wpbp_deleted_option', 'fallback' ); return 'fallback' === $result && false === get_option( 'wpbp_deleted_option', false );
assertions.description: The option is deleted and get_option returns the supplied fallback

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_005( string $name, mixed $fallback ): mixed { delete_option( $name ); return get_option( $name, $fallback ); }

tests.prompt: A site checks stock through the slow helper wpbp_stock_lookup_source( string $code ), which answers true (stocked), false (not stocked) or null (no such product) and must run at most once per code. Implement a function that returns that same three-state answer for a code and caches it as a transient named 'wpbp_stock_' followed by the code for five minutes, so the second call for the same code answers from the cache with an identical value.
tests.expected_behavior: Transients round-trip through the options table, so a stored `false` or `null` comes back as an empty string and `get_transient()` returns false for both a miss and a cached negative. The answer therefore has to be stored in a wrapper (an array, or a normalized string) that keeps the three states apart. Runtime validation calls each of the three codes twice and requires strictly identical results with exactly one helper invocation per code, plus a transient timeout about five minutes out.
requirements: Call wpbp_stock_lookup_source() at most once per product code
Cache the answer as a transient named 'wpbp_stock_' followed by the code, expiring after five minutes
Return exactly the same three-state answer (true, false or null) whether it came from the helper or from the cache

required_patterns.description: Stores the answer as a transient

runtime_checks.setup: foreach ( array( 'wpbp_stock_in-stock', 'wpbp_stock_sold-out', 'wpbp_stock_unknown-code' ) as $key ) { delete_transient( $key ); } $GLOBALS['wpbp_so_006_calls'] = array(); if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_stock_lookup_source' ) ) { function wpbp_stock_lookup_source( string $code ) { $GLOBALS['wpbp_so_006_calls'][] = $code; if ( 'in-stock' === $code ) { return true; } if ( 'sold-out' === $code ) { return false; } return null; } }

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_006' ) ) { return false; } $GLOBALS['wpbp_so_006_calls'] = array(); $expected = array( 'sold-out' => false, 'unknown-code' => null, 'in-stock' => true ); $seen = array(); foreach ( $expected as $code => $answer ) { $first = wpbp_settings_options_006( $code ); if ( $answer !== $first ) { return false; } $seen[] = $code; if ( $seen !== $GLOBALS['wpbp_so_006_calls'] ) { return false; } $second = wpbp_settings_options_006( $code ); if ( $answer !== $second ) { return false; } if ( $seen !== $GLOBALS['wpbp_so_006_calls'] ) { return false; } } global $wpdb; $timeout = (int) $wpdb->get_var( $wpdb->prepare( "SELECT option_value FROM {$wpdb->options} WHERE option_name = %s", '_transient_timeout_wpbp_stock_sold-out' ) ); return $timeout > time() && $timeout <= time() + 600;
assertions.description: Each code is looked up once and every cached answer keeps its exact three-state value

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_006( string $code ) { $key = 'wpbp_stock_' . $code; $cached = get_transient( $key ); if ( is_array( $cached ) && array_key_exists( 'stocked', $cached ) ) { return $cached['stocked']; } $stocked = wpbp_stock_lookup_source( $code ); set_transient( $key, array( 'stocked' => $stocked ), 5 * MINUTE_IN_SECONDS ); return $stocked; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_settings_options_006( string $code ) { $key = 'wpbp_stock_' . $code; $cached = get_transient( $key ); if ( false !== $cached ) { return $cached; } $stocked = wpbp_stock_lookup_source( $code ); set_transient( $key, $stocked, 5 * MINUTE_IN_SECONDS ); return $stocked; }

function wpbp_settings_options_006( string $code ) { $key = 'wpbp_stock_' . $code; $cached = get_transient( $key ); if ( ! empty( $cached ) ) { return $cached; } $stocked = wpbp_stock_lookup_source( $code ); set_transient( $key, $stocked, 5 * MINUTE_IN_SECONDS ); return $stocked; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that applies a map of option name to desired autoload flag in a single pass over the options table, and returns a map of option name to whether that option's stored autoload value actually had to change.
tests.expected_behavior: The function delegates to `wp_set_option_autoload_values()`, which selects the options whose autoload value differs and issues at most two UPDATE queries, returning `true` only for the options it changed. Runtime validation seeds one autoloaded option to switch off, one already-off option requested off, and one autoloaded option requested on; the returned map must be `true`, `false`, `false`, the stored autoload column must read `off`, `off`, `on`, and the whole call must stay within a small query budget so a per-option loop fails.
requirements: Accept a map of option name to desired autoload flag (true to autoload, false to not autoload)
Apply the whole map in one pass rather than one option at a time — the call must not cost more than a handful of database queries
Return a map of option name to true when the stored autoload value changed and false when it was already correct

runtime_checks.setup: global $wpdb; $seed = array( 'wpbp_autoload_on' => 'on', 'wpbp_autoload_off' => 'off', 'wpbp_autoload_keep' => 'on' ); foreach ( $seed as $name => $flag ) { delete_option( $name ); add_option( $name, 'value for ' . $name, '', 'on' === $flag ); $wpdb->update( $wpdb->options, array( 'autoload' => $flag ), array( 'option_name' => $name ) ); } wp_cache_flush();

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_007' ) ) { return false; } global $wpdb; wp_cache_flush(); $baseline = (int) $wpdb->num_queries; $result = wpbp_settings_options_007( array( 'wpbp_autoload_on' => false, 'wpbp_autoload_off' => false, 'wpbp_autoload_keep' => true ) ); $queries = (int) $wpdb->num_queries - $baseline; if ( ! is_array( $result ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== ( $result['wpbp_autoload_on'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== ( $result['wpbp_autoload_off'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== ( $result['wpbp_autoload_keep'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } if ( $queries > 4 ) { return false; } $rows = $wpdb->get_results( "SELECT option_name, autoload FROM {$wpdb->options} WHERE option_name IN ( 'wpbp_autoload_on', 'wpbp_autoload_off', 'wpbp_autoload_keep' )", OBJECT_K ); if ( 3 !== count( $rows ) ) { return false; } return 'off' === $rows['wpbp_autoload_on']->autoload && 'off' === $rows['wpbp_autoload_off']->autoload && 'on' === $rows['wpbp_autoload_keep']->autoload;
assertions.description: Only the option that needed a change reports true, the stored flags are correct, and the batch stays within its query budget

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_007( array $autoload_map ): array { return wp_set_option_autoload_values( $autoload_map ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_settings_options_007( array $autoload_map ): array { $results = array(); foreach ( $autoload_map as $option => $autoload ) { $results[ $option ] = wp_set_option_autoload( $option, $autoload ); } return $results; }
function wpbp_settings_options_007( array $autoload_map ): array { $results = array(); foreach ( $autoload_map as $option => $autoload ) { $results[ $option ] = (bool) $autoload; } return $results; }

tests.prompt: The option 'wpbp_theme_mode' has never been saved. Register a fallback so that reading it without a default yields 'auto', while a caller that supplies its own default still gets exactly what it asked for (including false), and a value saved later wins over the fallback.
tests.expected_behavior: The code hooks `default_option_wpbp_theme_mode` and uses the third filter argument (`$passed_default`) to tell 'no default supplied' from 'a default was supplied', returning `'auto'` only in the former case. Runtime validation reads the option with no default, with 'dark', with false, then saves 'light' and reads it back both ways, and checks an unrelated missing option is untouched.
requirements: Reading 'wpbp_theme_mode' with no default must yield 'auto'
A caller-supplied default must be returned unchanged, including when that default is false
A value saved to the option must take precedence over the fallback
Other options must not be affected

assertions.code: if ( 'auto' !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'dark' !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode', 'dark' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode', false ) ) { return false; } if ( 'x' !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_other', 'x' ) ) { return false; } if ( false !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_other' ) ) { return false; } if ( true !== update_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode', 'light' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'light' !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'light' !== get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode', 'dark' ) ) { return false; } delete_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode' ); return 'auto' === get_option( 'wpbp_theme_mode' );
assertions.description: The fallback applies only when no default was passed, and a saved value wins

tests.prompt: A plugin screen needs the values of several options that are not autoloaded. Implement a function that, given a list of option names, returns a map of option name to value while hitting the database only once for the whole list, no matter how many names are supplied. Names with no stored option must map to false.
tests.expected_behavior: The function calls `wp_prime_option_caches()` with the whole list so a single query loads them all into the options cache (and records the missing one in `notoptions`), then reads each value with `get_option()`, which is served from cache. Runtime validation flushes the cache, counts queries around the call, and checks the values, including an array-valued option and a missing one.
requirements: Return a map of option name to option value, preserving each option's stored type
Load the whole list with a single database query rather than one query per option
Map option names that do not exist to false

required_patterns.description: Primes the whole list in one query
Reads the primed values through the Options API

runtime_checks.setup: $seed = array( 'wpbp_prime_a' => 'alpha', 'wpbp_prime_b' => 'bravo', 'wpbp_prime_c' => 'charlie', 'wpbp_prime_d' => array( 'nested' => 'delta' ), 'wpbp_prime_e' => '0' ); foreach ( $seed as $name => $value ) { delete_option( $name ); add_option( $name, $value, '', false ); } delete_option( 'wpbp_prime_missing' ); wp_cache_flush();

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_009' ) ) { return false; } global $wpdb; $names = array( 'wpbp_prime_a', 'wpbp_prime_b', 'wpbp_prime_c', 'wpbp_prime_d', 'wpbp_prime_e', 'wpbp_prime_missing' ); wp_cache_flush(); $baseline = (int) $wpdb->num_queries; $values = wpbp_settings_options_009( $names ); $queries = (int) $wpdb->num_queries - $baseline; if ( ! is_array( $values ) || $queries > 3 ) { return false; } $expected = array( 'wpbp_prime_a' => 'alpha', 'wpbp_prime_b' => 'bravo', 'wpbp_prime_c' => 'charlie', 'wpbp_prime_e' => '0' ); foreach ( $expected as $name => $value ) { if ( ! array_key_exists( $name, $values ) || $value !== $values[ $name ] ) { return false; } } if ( array( 'nested' => 'delta' ) !== ( $values['wpbp_prime_d'] ?? null ) ) { return false; } return array_key_exists( 'wpbp_prime_missing', $values ) && false === $values['wpbp_prime_missing'];
assertions.description: All six values are returned correctly from a single priming query

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_009( array $option_names ): array { wp_prime_option_caches( $option_names ); $values = array(); foreach ( $option_names as $name ) { $values[ $name ] = get_option( $name ); } return $values; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_settings_options_009( array $option_names ): array { $values = array(); foreach ( $option_names as $name ) { $values[ $name ] = get_option( $name ); } return $values; }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that saves a value to a named option and reports which of three things happened: the option did not exist and was created, it existed and now holds a different value, or it already held exactly that value so nothing was written. Return 'created', 'updated' or 'unchanged'. Options whose stored value is an empty string or '0' still count as existing.
tests.expected_behavior: The function must not read a plain `get_option()` result as an existence test (an option holding '' or '0' looks missing) and must not read `update_option()` returning false as a failure (false also means 'value unchanged'). The reliable shape is an existence probe with a unique default before writing, then `update_option()`. Runtime validation exercises a missing option, an identical rewrite, a changed value, an option stored as '0', and an option stored as an empty string.
requirements: Return exactly one of the strings 'created', 'updated' or 'unchanged'
Treat an option whose stored value is '' or '0' as existing
Write the value through the Options API

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_settings_options_010' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'created' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_new', 'alpha' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'alpha' !== get_option( 'wpbp_state_new' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'unchanged' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_new', 'alpha' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'updated' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_new', 'beta' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'beta' !== get_option( 'wpbp_state_new' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'unchanged' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_zero', '0' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'updated' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_zero', '1' ) ) { return false; } if ( 'unchanged' !== wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_empty', '' ) ) { return false; } return 'updated' === wpbp_settings_options_010( 'wpbp_state_empty', 'gamma' ) && 'gamma' === get_option( 'wpbp_state_empty' );
assertions.description: Creation, no-op writes and real changes are reported apart, including for falsy stored values

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_settings_options_010( string $option, $value ): string { $sentinel = '__wpbp_absent_' . wp_generate_uuid4(); $existed = $sentinel !== get_option( $option, $sentinel ); $changed = update_option( $option, $value ); if ( ! $changed ) { return 'unchanged'; } return $existed ? 'updated' : 'created'; }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_settings_options_010( string $option, $value ): string { return update_option( $option, $value ) ? 'updated' : 'unchanged'; }

function wpbp_settings_options_010( string $option, $value ): string { $existed = (bool) get_option( $option ); if ( ! update_option( $option, $value ) ) { return 'unchanged'; } return $existed ? 'updated' : 'created'; }
